requirements.requirement: Configure /srv/releases as a shared release-team workspace.
requirements.summary: The release-team group exists, and /srv/releases is a directory owned by root:release-team with mode 2775, providing group write access and setgid behavior. The same configuration was directly verified after restart and after cleanup.

requirements.requirement: New files created in /srv/releases inherit the release-team group.
requirements.summary: Files created both before and after the node restart were directly observed with group release-team. The verification files were subsequently removed.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also coherent: it records the healthy pre-restart workspace and boot identity, restart acknowledgement, an observed outage, a different post-restart boot identity, persisted test data, restored configuration, and successful post-restart inheritance. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently confirm the boot change.
limitations: Native package-manager consistency checks timed out both before and after execution, so package health was not independently observed (global:before_prepare:node1:package-health; global:after_executor:node1:package-health). No package-changing commands appear in the complete executor timeline.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Workspace creation and permission changes directly implemented the task; temporary files provided bounded functional and persistence evidence; the reboot fulfilled the mandatory restart protocol; and cleanup removed both probes. Failed polling commands were read-only checks during the expected restart outage. Final observations show no failed services, no new listening endpoints, and only normal per-boot systemd temporary-directory changes.
